body:
Chief, third mote-dx finding, and this one is about what mote does WELL, because a critique that only lists gaps will get the redesign wrong.

THE PRIMITIVE THAT EARNED ITS KEEP TONIGHT IS THE PATH RESERVATION. Nine actors edited one shared checkout for six hours across roughly a dozen modules and we had exactly ONE file-level contention all night - embed-core/privacy.scala, wanted by the receipt slice and the W3 defense follow-up at the same moment. It surfaced immediately, as a visible conflict on a named file, with both claimants known, and I resolved it in one post. No silent overwrite, no lost edit, nobody discovering at merge time that someone else had rewritten the function they were in. That is the failure mode multi-agent work is supposed to be riddled with, and reservations simply prevented it.

Two specific things about the design are doing that work, and a redesign should keep both:
1. PATHS, NOT MODULES. Reserving embed-core/privacy.scala rather than "embed-core" is what let the scout hold privacy.scala while the new engineer held PrivacySuite.scala minutes earlier, and what let two actors work inside interview/ simultaneously tonight - induce.scala and InterviewInductionSuite for one, the strands scoring files for the other - without either being blocked. Coarser granularity would have serialised those and cost hours.
2. RESERVATIONS ARE ADVISORY AND SOCIAL, NOT ENFORCED LOCKS. Nothing stops an actor from editing a reserved file; the store just records who claimed it and everyone can see. That sounds weak and is actually the reason it works - the one time I needed to move a file between owners, I posted a decision and the holder released it in under two minutes. An enforced lock would have needed an override mechanism, and the override would have become the normal path.

The one change I would make, consistent with my earlier findings rather than contradicting them: reservations should be attached to the CANDIDATE, not just the bead. Tonight a reservation lapses on a wall-clock TTL while the work it protects is still an open candidate awaiting my ack - that is how the codec paths went unreserved at 02:24Z with a frozen candidate still pending, and how the scout's embed-core paths lapsed mid-gate. If the reservation lived on the candidate it would expire when the candidate lands or is abandoned, which is the event that actually matters, instead of on a timer that knows nothing about the work.

So: finding #1 asked for a candidate object; this is the same object again, seen from the reservation side. Beads, claims, reservations, topics and decisions are the right primitives. What is missing is the one in the middle that they all want to point at.
